messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after the kernel selector flip at 10:12 PT we saw a p95 regression on /generate-route. tails went to ~210ms vs 150ms SLO. attaching profiler snippet and heap of quick notes.

anil: noted. initial glance: KV cache miss rate jumped from 86% -> 62% for that route, and batch formation skewed towards lots of tiny minibatches (~2-4 requests). could be batcher gating + kernel handoff timing. :thinking:

cheng: can you paste the small perf dump? I want to check microbatch distribution and whether the new kernel prefers larger seq lengths.

maria: pasted below — the important bits are the arrival histogram and kernel switch log.

maria: ```
arrival_histogram: {0-10ms: 56%, 10-30ms: 30%, >30ms:14%}
kernel_switch: selected kernel "kern_v2_fast_attn" at 10:12:03 for seq<=512
batcher_state: {active_minibatches: 128, avg_minibatch_size: 3.2, kv_hit_ratio: 0.62}
log: [10:12:02] prefetch triggered for route_id=generate-route tier=gold
     [10:12:03] kernel_swizzle: kern_v1 -> kern_v2 timeout=12ms
```

anil: ok — two hypotheses: (1) kern_v2 has slightly worse single-token latency for small microbatches due to its input layout, (2) prefetch gating or budgeter reduced token budgets per route causing earlier flushes.

denise: remind me — what are the current dynamic token budget targets for gold vs silver? Iirc we were using a formula that scales with p50 latency and batch occupancy.

maria: current live canary config snippet: 
```json
{"budgeter":{"per_tier":{"gold":32,"silver":24,"bronze":12},"min_batch_size":8,"max_tokens_per_batch":4096}}
```

anil: that min_batch_size=8 is important — the batcher will try to fill to 8 before dispatch unless p95 timer fires. if kernel_v2 increases single-token cost, the timer threshold might be firing earlier causing many 3-4 sized batches despite min target.

cheng: also worth checking KV cache TTL skew — if cache warms slower after kernel switchover we get more full-sequence compute rather than prefix reuse. check KV eviction counts.

maria: eviction delta: +18% in that minute window. KV cold-starts correlate with route-level affinity shift after switchover.

denise: pragmatic next steps?

maria: propose short checklist: 
- revert kernel selector to kern_v1 for the route as quick rollback (ops-bot can do).
- run a canary with adjusted budgeter: lower min_batch_size to 4 and increase per_tier budgets by 25% for gold.
- enable additional KV prewarm for generate-route for 5m during canary.
- collect microbatch histograms and p95 for 15m windows.

anil: agree. alternative: keep kern_v2 but change the queue policy to favor waiting up to 12ms for extra tokens for gold tier only (hedge wait). could preserve throughput.

cheng: pseudo-config for the hedge wait approach: 
```
{"queue_policy":{"tier_overrides":{"gold":{"wait_ms":12,"max_wait_ms":20}},"fallback":"default"}}
```

maria: ops-bot, can you schedule a rollback to kern_v1 for route generate-route on 10:35 PT if we don't approve canary? tag: @denise @anil

ops-bot: scheduled rollback job #RB-4531 at 10:35 PT unless cancelled. :white_check_mark:

denise: i'll approve a canary with config changes for 10:20 PT. anil/cheng please prepare the perf checklist and queries.

anil: prepping queries now — perf counters I need: minibatch_size_distribution, kv_hit_ratio_by_route, kernel_latency_by_batch_size. will push dashboards and a short logstash query.

cheng: i'll add kernel-level counters: op_cost_per_tok, memcopy_latency, and also output the kernel selector scoring weights.

maria: quick note on telemetry naming: use tag "hedge-wait-canary-429" for logs and dashboards so we can filter.

denise: timeline: canary at 10:20, observe 15m windows, decision by 10:40 -> rollback auto at 10:35 if no action (ops-bot set). updates in thread. :shipit:

maria: thanks — i'll post 10:36 p95 numbers here. if we still see >160ms p95 we'll revert.

anil: one more idea for longer term: add a kernel_cost_estimator signal into batch shaping so budgeter uses expected per-token cost times pending tokens to decide to wait vs flush. reduces surprise from kernel swaps.

maria: love that. logging done.

ops-bot: canary deploy started: cfg_id=hedge-wait-canary-429, targets=[generate-route:gold], start_ts=4298765440

maria: canary running. initial p50 looks fine, p95 trending down from 210->170 after 3 minutes, kv_hit_ratio slowly recovering.

anil: initial microbatch sizes increasing to avg 5.9 (good). keep an eye on latency tail at 10m mark.

cheng: dumping kernel selector weights for trace id X-992: "latency_penalty":0.12, "throughput_bonus":0.03, "prefers_large_batches":true

maria: 10:36 snapshot: p95=158ms, avg_minibatch_size=6.1, kv_hit_ratio=0.78. looks promising.

denise: good. hold canary and we can graduate the config after an hour if stable. documenting follow-ups: (a) implement kernel_cost_estimator, (b) add route-level KV prewarm on kernel flips, (c) add a route-tier anomaly alert for rapid kv_hit_ratio drops.

maria: noted — will open follow-up tickets and link here. thanks all! :tada:
